newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Gillette estimates cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Gillette estimates cut.

text.p: Morgan Stanley, CS First Boston and Merrill Lynch lowered their 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates on the shares of Gillette Co on Friday after the giant consumer products company guided estimates lower.
-- Gillette said it guided analysts' estimates down, citing performance at its Braun unit, which makes shaving supplies and small appliances.
-- Morgan Stanley analyst Brenda Landry said she reduced her 1997 earnings estimate to $2.55 per share from $2.60 per share and her 1998 estimate to $3.00 from $3.05 per share.

-- Gillette said its Braun unit was hurt by weakness in Japan and Germany, two key markets for the operation. It said it guided analysts to the lower end of an earlier range of $2.55 to $2.60 per share for 1997 earnings.
-- Morgan Stanley's Landry said she recommended using any weakness in the shares as a buying opportunity. She reiterated her strong buy on the stock.
-- "The company is still a 17 to 18 percent grower which is trying to accomplish a lot in 1997," she said, adding that Gillette was also trying to digest the Duracell acquisition.

-- Merrill Lynch said it cut its 1997 estimate on the stock to $2.55 per share from a range of $2.55 to $2.60 per share, and it cut its 1998 estimate to $3.00 per share from a $3.05 to $3.10 per share.
-- Merrill Lynch kept its intermediate-term accumulate rating and long-term buy rating on the stock.
-- CS First Boston also cut its 1997 estimate by a nickel to $2.55 per share and its 1998 estimate to $3.00 from $3.05 per share.
-- CS First Boston rated Gillette a buy.
